walkthroughs.body_html:
Medieval people had no idea about germs.

Many thought God was punishing them for their sins. Others blamed the planets — bad alignments of stars and planets. Many believed in miasma, or bad air rising from rotting waste.

Sadly, many also blamed and attacked Jewish communities, especially in Europe. 😢

Doctors followed the old idea of the Four Humours — blood, phlegm, black bile and yellow bile. To balance them they used bloodletting, sometimes with leeches.

People also tried:

  • Burning sweet herbs to clean the 'bad air'
  • Carrying a posy of flowers to the nose
  • Praying, fasting and going on processions
  • The flagellants — groups who whipped themselves in public

None of it stopped the plague.

So many died that normal funerals were impossible. Bodies were buried in huge plague pits.

Whole villages were wiped out — some 'lost villages' you can still see today as bumps in fields.

The rhyme 'Ring a ring o' roses' is sometimes linked to the plague, though historians are not sure. By 1350 the worst was over — but it returned in waves for centuries.

mcqs.q: Was the 1923 Munich Putsch a complete failure for Hitler?
options: The Munich Putsch succeeded in overthrowing the Bavarian government for several weeks.
Slavery was abolished because cotton was no longer profitable.
Militarily yes — it collapsed in hours — but the trial gave Hitler a national platform and he wrote Mein Kampf in prison, learning to pursue power legally instead.
The Munich Putsch destroyed the Nazi Party until Hitler rebuilt it from nothing.
A combination of moral campaigning, slave resistance and rebellions (especially Haiti and Jamaica), and the shifting economic interest of industrial capitalism.
The October Revolution overthrew the Tsar.
Wilberforce single-handedly persuaded Parliament to end slavery out of pure morality.
Slavery was abolished because cotton was no longer profitable.

mcqs.q: How did the Bolsheviks seize power in October 1917?
options: The October Revolution overthrew the Tsar.
The October Revolution was a mass popular uprising that stormed the Winter Palace.
The Munich Putsch succeeded in overthrowing the Bavarian government for several weeks.
Trotsky's Military Revolutionary Committee coordinated a near-bloodless takeover of key buildings in Petrograd from a Provisional Government that had lost army and worker support.
